ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, A, B, C, D, and E are on the same horizontal line segment, and B, C, and D mark AE into four equal small segments. The upper path is a semicircular arc with AE as the diameter; the lower path consists of two semicircular arcs: one is the larger lower semicircular arc with AD as the diameter, and the other is the small lower semicircular arc with DE as the diameter. Then reason: Let the length of each small segment be x, then AE = 4x, AD = 3x, DE = x. The length of a semicircular arc with diameter d is half the circumference, namely πd/2. So the upper path length is π(4x)/2 = 2πx. The lower path length is π(3x)/2 + π(x)/2 = 3πx/2 + πx/2 = 2πx. Therefore the lengths of the upper and lower paths are equal, and the ratio is 2πx : 2πx = 1 : 1.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A, B, C, D, E lie on one horizontal segment, with the upper path shown as the semicircular arc from A to E using AE as diameter. The lower path shown consists of the lower semicircular arc from A to D using AD as diameter, followed by the small lower semicircular arc from D to E using DE as diameter. From the text, AE is divided into four equal parts, so if each part has length x, then AE = 4x, AD = 3x, and DE = x. Use the semicircle arc length formula: arc length = half the circumference = πd/2 for diameter d. Thus upper path length = π(4x)/2 = 2πx. Lower path length = π(3x)/2 + π(x)/2 = 2πx. Therefore the ratio of upper path to lower path is 2πx : 2πx = 1 : 1.
